justification_text:
My point estimates reflect a modestly upward-drifting baseline from an assumed current price near 125. At the one-day horizon, the estimate of 125.2 essentially assumes mean-reversion and continuity — overnight and intraday noise tends to average out, and absent a specific catalyst, prices rarely move dramatically in a single session. For the one-week estimate of 125.8, I incorporated a slight positive drift consistent with a broad assumption of mild bullish momentum or a neutral-to-positive macro backdrop, while acknowledging that a week provides enough time for a few meaningful trading sessions to compound small moves. The one-month estimate of 127.0 extrapolates that gentle drift further, essentially pricing in steady but unspectacular appreciation without assuming any major fundamental re-rating.

The confidence interval widths widen progressively across horizons in a way that reflects the classic square-root-of-time scaling of uncertainty. At one day, the 90% interval of roughly plus or minus 2.7 points captures typical daily volatility — perhaps a 2% range — which is consistent with a moderately volatile asset. By one week, the interval widens to about plus or minus 6.3 points, reflecting multiple days of compounding uncertainty. At one month, the interval of plus or minus 14 points incorporates the reality that over four-plus weeks, macroeconomic data releases, earnings, policy decisions, and sentiment shifts can meaningfully alter the trajectory. I also allowed for some skew at longer horizons since assets can gap lower faster than they rise in risk-off environments.

Several specific risks could push outcomes outside these stated intervals. On the upside, a surprise positive catalyst — such as a better-than-expected earnings report, a dovish central bank pivot, or a resolution of a geopolitical overhang — could push prices well above 132 at the one-week horizon or beyond 141 at one month. On the downside, a sudden risk-off episode driven by unexpected inflation data, a credit event, or geopolitical escalation could drive prices sharply below 119 within a week or below 113 within a month. Liquidity conditions matter too: in thin markets, moves can overshoot fair value considerably, making the tails fatter than the intervals imply.

It is also worth noting that my intervals assume roughly stationary volatility, which is itself a simplification. Volatility can cluster — a spike in realized volatility today tends to persist — and if conditions become more turbulent after this forecast was made, even the one-day interval could prove too narrow.
